checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: 10M activities recording at 1 Hz. Where do the in-progress GPS points go?

options.label: Append to Postgres
options.verdict: 10M rows/sec into a B-tree, and almost all of it gets rewritten into a summary the moment the athlete stops. You are paying durable-store prices for data that is scratch until the activity ends.

options.label: Hot in-memory buffer per activity
options.verdict: The in-progress track is scratch space. Buffer it and write one compact record at the end — 3,600 writes become one, and the durable store only ever sees finished activities.

defend.prompt: What did you accept by buffering?

options.label: An athlete can lose the tail of an in-progress activity
You need periodic checkpointing to bound that loss
Live segment leaderboards now read from the buffer, not the DB

defend.explain: Finished activities are written through and unaffected. The exposure is only the unflushed window, which is why you checkpoint every few minutes rather than only at stop.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: 10M concurrent activities, 1 Hz sampling, ~50 bytes per point.

rungs.note: One point per activity per second.
10M x 50 bytes. Compression on the wire matters at this rate.
~180 KB per hour-long activity x 10M/day, before indexes.

checkpoints.explain: 500 MB/s of ingest that compresses to a fraction once an activity is closed. The design pressure is the write rate, not the eventual storage.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.prompt: Build the ingest path for a live activity point.
checkpoints.explain: Points land in a per-activity Redis buffer so the hot path never touches disk. Kafka carries completed activities onward for durable storage and asynchronous segment matching — deliberately off the ingest path, because a slow leaderboard must never stall a recording.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: Activity uploads succeed, but segment leaderboards are hours stale.
checkpoints.explain: Ingest is healthy, which is why uploads feel fine. Segment matching is a consumer of the same stream and it has fallen 12M messages behind — the CPU-heavy geometry match cannot keep up with 10M concurrent activities. Scale the matcher consumers or pre-filter candidate segments by bounding box before matching.

wrong.Redis buffer: 61% memory is comfortable. The buffer is doing its job.
wrong.Ingest Service: 30ms p99 — the write path is not where the delay is.
wrong.Postgres: Postgres is keeping up with what reaches it; the backlog is upstream.
